title: Nepal rescuers drill into tunnels in bid to reach trapped workers - Al Jazeera
description: Nepal rescuers drill into tunnels in bid to reach trapped workers  Al Jazeera
publisher.title: Al Jazeera
full_article:
Nepali rescuers seeking to reach hydropower workers believed trapped in tunnels swamped by flood debris have resumed work after rain and rising river waters hampered efforts.

Nepal’s government says more than 100 workers may still be alive and trapped inside multiple tunnels at hydropower projects, with key rescue efforts focused on the Trishuli 3A and 3B sites.

Recommended Stories list of 3 items list 1 of 3 Chinese rescuers race to reach mudslide survivors in Nepal-China border

Chinese rescuers race to reach mudslide survivors in Nepal-China border list 2 of 3 Anger mounts in Nepal over the government’s response to flash flood

Anger mounts in Nepal over the government’s response to flash flood list 3 of 3 Isolated by raging floodwaters, Nepal’s miracle home amid the devastation end of list

Huge flash floods triggered on Wednesday when part of a glacier collapsed near Nepal’s border with Tibet have left at least 750 people dead and more than 3,000 missing.

Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority says there are 933 hydropower workers among the missing.

At Trishuli 3A in Nepal’s Rasuwa District on Saturday evening, army rescue teams using drills broke through into the upper part of a mud-swamped tunnel and began pumping air as well as sending in a camera.

But overnight rain and rising river waters hampered efforts early on Sunday, filling the excavation area with water before conditions eased.

“As the floodwaters have receded, the team has resumed efforts to locate the tunnel entrance using drilling machines, excavators, hydraulic cutters and other equipment,” said a Nepal Army statement on Sunday.

Al Jazeera’s Minelle Fernandez, reporting from the Nepalese capital, Kathmandu, said the government has requested specialist help from India and China to “fill gaps” in its rescue operations.

“The government is trying to give it its best shot, bringing in these experts to see if there is any way or means of bringing out anyone who is still alive,” she said.

Advertisement

The catastrophe on Wednesday was triggered when part of a glacier at roughly 5,200 metres high in the Himalayas collapsed, plunging about 1,200 metres and gathering rock and debris before slamming into the Lende River.

The resulting surge swept south through Nepal’s Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading districts, at one point raising the Trishuli River by nine metres in 30 minutes. The US Geological Survey revised its initial finding of an earthquake trigger, concluding the seismic signal instead came from the landslide itself.

A woman waits to identify her husband at a temporary holding centre in Bharatpur where the bodies of flash flood victims are being kept, August 30, 2026 [Navesh Chitrakar/Reuters]

Al Jazeera’s Jessica Washington, reporting from Dhading, said the river had receded on Sunday, but the current remained strong.

She said the floodwaters had destroyed many homes, leaving behind only the foundations. Those still standing are “in a state of complete disrepair,” she said.

“Speaking to some residents, this [disaster] represents not only the destruction of their homes, but their livelihoods as well because many of the residents told us that they had small stores and small businesses in the bottom floors of their homes and all of their products – everything – has been completely washed away.”

Nepal’s National Disaster Management Authority said on Sunday that 734 bodies had been recovered. The number of missing on the Nepalese side of the border is at least 2,498.

Chinese authorities have reported that the death toll in Tibet has increased to 16, with 546 people missing. Al Jazeera’s Katrina Yu, reporting from Beijing, said 261 foreigners from 23 countries are among those unaccounted for.

Countries pledge support

International aid has arrived from the United Nations, the Red Cross Federation, Australia, India, South Korea and the United States.

The US and Canada said they would provide $3.6m each in humanitarian aid. The United Kingdom has offered $6.8m in aid, while the UN released $2.5m in emergency funding.

On Friday, the European Union pledged $2.3m and the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) said it had allocated more than $1m and launched an emergency appeal for $31m.

Al Jazeera’s Samer Allawi said authorities “have not yet moved to the second phase of relief operations, which includes humanitarian assistance and reopening roads”, because of “the rugged terrain and the lack of sufficient resources”.

He said that Nepal’s finance minister estimated losses from the disaster at “more than $4bn”, while warnings remain in place over possible flooding along rivers in northern Nepal.

हुनी कहलकै कि नेपाल केरऽ वित्त मंत्री न॑ ई आपदा स॑ नुकसान के अनुमान “४ अरब डॉलर स॑ भी अधिक” लगैलकै, जबकि उत्तरी नेपाल म॑ नदी के किनारे संभावित बाढ़ के बारे म॑ चेतावनी जारी छै ।

Rescue and relief efforts in Nepal and Tibet have been hampered this Sunday by heavy rain and rising river levels. The latest figures following Wednesday’s flash floods put the death toll at 750, while more than 3,000 people remain missing. Nepal’s disaster authorities are urging rescue teams to “exercise caution”, warning that bad weather, swollen rivers and the threat of further flooding could hamper operations. Shazab Wahlah reports from the town of Bidur.

title: WHO releases US$150 000 emergency funds to support Nepal’s flood response - World Health Organization (WHO)

full_article:
The World Health Organization has released US$150 000 from the South-East Asia Regional Health Emergency Fund (SEARHEF) to support urgent health and other needs of the communities impacted by the devastating flash floods in Nepal, one of the worst tragedies in the country in recent times.

“The emergency funds will support immediate response priorities. WHO is committed to supporting Nepal through the response and recovery efforts,” said Dr Nilesh Buddha, Officer-in-Charge, WHO South-East Asia Regional Office.

Earlier, within hours of the flash floods on 26 August, WHO mobilized and dispatched essential emergency medical supplies, including an Interagency Emergency Health Kit that can cater to the health needs of nearly 10 000 people for 3 months, along with multipurpose tents.

Based on urgent needs, WHO further mobilized surgical masks and gloves, hand sanitizers and other medical supplies for the affected areas.

Over 730 people have been killed in the floods, nearly 2500 are missing, over 200 are injured, and 74 are undergoing treatment, as per the latest report released by national authorities.

An estimated 10 000 households need immediate relief in six districts across Bagmati and Gandaki provinces, severely affected by the floods. Widespread loss of life, displacement and damage to critical infrastructure, including health facilities are being reported. Four health facilities in the worst hit Rasuwa district have been completely damaged and two in Dhading are partially damaged. Two hospitals – in Dhading and Trishuli – are inaccessible as roads are damaged. Reaching displaced population in access compromised areas continues to be a challenge.

WHO is working closely with the Government and partners to coordinate the health response, strengthen disease surveillance, maintain essential health services and identify and address emerging health risks. These include drowning, injuries, diarrhoeal and respiratory illnesses, water- and food-borne diseases, and vector-borne diseases among others. The loss of loved ones, homes and livelihoods, along with displacement and uncertainty, can also have a significant impact on mental health and psychosocial well-being of the affected communities.

About SEARHEF

The South-East Asia Regional Health Emergency Fund (SEARHEF) is WHO's regional flagship mechanism for providing rapid and flexible financing for timely emergency response and strengthened preparedness across the WHO South-East Asia Region. The Nepal allocation marks the 54th health emergency supported by SEARHEF since its inception in 2008.

‘आपातकालीन कोष स तत्काल प्रतिक्रिया प्राथमिकता मे सहयोग भेटत, डब्ल्यूएचओ प्रतिक्रिया आ पुनर्प्राप्ति प्रयास क माध्यम स नेपाल कए सहयोग करबा लेल प्रतिबद्ध अछि।’ डब्ल्यूएचओ दक्षिण पूर्व एशिया क्षेत्रीय कार्यालय क प्रभारी अधिकारी डॉ नीलेश बुद्ध कहला।

एहि सं पहिने 26 अगस्त के फ्लैश फ्लड के घंटों के भीतर डब्ल्यूएचओ जरूरी आपातकालीन चिकित्सा आपूर्ति के जुटान केलक आ भेजलक, जाहि मे एकटा इंटरएजेंसी इमरजेंसी हेल्थ किट शामिल अछि जे 3 महीना तक लगभग 10 000 लोक के स्वास्थ्य जरूरत के पूरा क सकैत अछि, संगहि बहुउद्देशीय टेंट सेहो.

तत्काल जरूरत के आधार पर डब्ल्यूएचओ न॑ आरू प्रभावित क्षेत्रऽ लेली सर्जिकल मास्क आरू दस्ताना, हैंड सेनेटाइजर आरू अन्य चिकित्सा आपूर्ति के जुटान करलकै ।

राष्ट्रीय प्राधिकरण द्वारा जारी ताजा रिपोर्ट के अनुसार बाढ़ि में 730 सं बेसी लोक के मौत भ गेल अछि, लगभग 2500 लापता अछि, 200 सं बेसी घायल भ गेल अछि, आ 74 के इलाज भ रहल अछि.

बाढ़ि सँ गंभीर रूप सँ प्रभावित बागमती आ गण्डकी प्रान्तक ६ जिला मे अनुमानित १० हजार घरके तत्काल राहतक आवश्यकता अछि । स्वास्थ्य सुविधा सहित महत्वपूर्ण बुनियादी ढाँचा के व्यापक नुकसान, विस्थापन आ नुकसान के खबर आबि रहल अछि. सबस बेसी प्रभावित रसुवा जिला मे चारिटा स्वास्थ्य सुविधा पूर्ण रूप स क्षतिग्रस्त भेल अछि आ धडिंग मे दूटा स्वास्थ्य सुविधा आंशिक रूप स क्षतिग्रस्त अछि। दूटा अस्पताल – धडिंग आ त्रिशूली मे – सड़क क्षतिग्रस्त भेला स दुर्गम अछि। पहुंच सं समझौता क्षेत्रक मे विस्थापित आबादी तक पहुंचनाय एकटा चुनौती बनल छै.

डब्ल्यूएचओ स्वास्थ्य प्रतिक्रिया कें समन्वय, रोगक कें निगरानी कें मजबूत करनाय, आवश्यक स्वास्थ्य सेवाक कें बनाए रखनाय आ उभरैत स्वास्थ्य जोखिम कें पहचान करनाय आ ओकरा सं निपटनाय कें लेल सरकार आ भागीदारक कें साथ मिलक क काज कयर रहल छै. अइ मे डूबनाय, चोट, दस्त आ श्वसन संबंधी बीमारियक, पानी आ भोजन सं होएय वाला बीमारियक, आ संवाहक सं होएय वाला बीमारियक आ अन्य शामिल छै. प्रियजन, घर आ आजीविका कें नुकसान कें साथ-साथ विस्थापन आ अनिश्चितता प्रभावित समुदायक कें मानसिक स्वास्थ्य आ मनोसामाजिक कल्याण पर सेहो काफी प्रभाव डाल सकय छै.

SEARHEF के बारे में

दक्षिण-पूर्व एशिया क्षेत्रीय स्वास्थ्य आपातकालीन कोष (SEARHEF) डब्ल्यूएचओ कें क्षेत्रीय प्रमुख तंत्र छै जे समय पर आपातकालीन प्रतिक्रिया आ पूरा डब्ल्यूएचओ दक्षिण-पूर्व एशिया क्षेत्र मे मजबूत तैयारी कें लेल तेजी सं आ लचीला वित्तपोषण प्रदान करय छै. नेपाल आवंटन 2008 मे शुरू भेला स सेयरहेफ द्वारा समर्थित 54म स्वास्थ्य आपातकाल अछि।

title: Fresh Flood Warnings Issued in Nepal: List Names ‘Out of Contact’ Americans - Newsweek
description: Fresh Flood Warnings Issued in Nepal: List Names ‘Out of Contact’ Americans  Newsweek
publisher.title: Newsweek
full_article:
Nepal authorities have warned of possible flooding throughout Sunday morning, as the Nepal Tourist Department shows a list of 64 Americans who are currently out of contact.

Residents in flood-affected districts have been urged to remain on high alert, after water levels in the Bhotekoshi River rose.

People received flood warnings on their phones throughout Sunday morning. Rescue crews are working to clear a major highway connecting Kathmandu to one of the areas that were worst hit by the catastrophic floods on Wednesday.

Read More on News

According to the latest information from Nepalese authorities, the combined death toll in Nepal and Tibet has risen to over 750, and more than 3,000 people are missing.

U.S. authorities said on Thursday that about 90 U.S. citizens were unaccounted for as of Thursday afternoon.

A list published by Nepal’s tourist department shows 64 Americans currently out of contact.

The list of those missing includes hundreds of people who were in the region to work, make a pilgrimage to a sacred peak or visit Nepal’s mountains.

Chinese state media said on Sunday that 261 foreigners were missing in Tibet.

How the Floods Unfolded

The flash floods on Wednesday began after a glacial collapse in the Himalayan region.

The disaster unfolded after an avalanche of ice and rock blocked a river, then unleashed a sudden surge downstream, according to officials and climate experts cited by The Associated Press .

...

The ensuing flood tore through villages, roads and hydropower projects in the Rasuwa district. The flooding then reached the Chinese side of the border.

The Rasuwa district experienced similar flooding in August of 2025. Then, a glacial lake in Tibet, the neighboring area, overflowed amid high temperatures in the mountain region.

Nine people were killed, and critical infrastructure was damaged, including a bridge connecting Nepal and China.

The Himalayan region is especially vulnerable to floods, heavy rainfall and landslides as it is warming faster than the rest of the world as a result of human-caused climate change.

Research by the Kathmandu-based organization International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development found that glacier ice loss across the vast mountainous Hindu Kush Himalaya (HKH) region has doubled since 2000, mainly because of rising global temperatures.

The HKH includes the 500-mile Hindu Kush system in Afghanistan and its ranges stretch approximately 2,175 miles across eight countries in Central and South Asia, including Pakistan, India, Nepal, Bhutan, China, Bangladesh and Myanmar, making it one of the most extensive and significant mountain systems in the world.

...

American Families Speak Out About Missing Loved Ones

The aftermath of the flooding has been devastating, and the uncertainty has been agonizing for families.

Jigisha Motwani, a Long Island resident whose family has known missing travelers Jitendra Patel and Amita Amin for decades, previously told Newsweek she was "gutted" when she learned they were among those unaccounted for.

Motwani said they are like an extended family. "I hope we can find a way to get in touch with them and bring them back," she said.

Manmeet Singh Meet, a close friend of Jiwan Jyoti, a Lexington resident listed as out of contact, told Newsweek he has known her for more than 15 years and is helping support her family as loved ones search for answers.

"It’s very heartbreaking," he said. "We are trying to get closure, to be very honest with you."

Authorities have yet to confirm whether those listed as out of contact are confirmed missing, injured, stranded or otherwise unable to communicate because of the disaster.

President Donald Trump and The State Department Address Nepal Flooding

The State Department said in a press release published on Wednesday: "The United States extends its deepest condolences to the families and loved ones of those who lost their lives in the devastating flash floods in the Rasuwa district of Nepal.

"Our thoughts are with all those affected by this disaster."

The department noted that it is monitoring the situation and has deployed a disaster response adviser to the region.

The State Department has provided $500,000 in assistance through the Catholic Relief Services.

Newsweek has contacted the State Department for further information outside of regular working hours.

...

While speaking to reporters on Thursday in the Oval Office, President Donald Trump said: "We’ve offered any help that they need.

"That was brutal. Nobody’s ever seen anything quite like that. Strong, well-built buildings were wiped out like they were toothpicks. It's a terrible thing. We are sending aid, and we've spoken to leadership, and we let them know anything they want will happen."

The president added that he didn't have a "full list" of the Americans who were in Nepal at the time.

"Hopefully they're OK, but that looked like something where somebody will be lost, unfortunately," he said.

नेपाल के अधिकारी सब रविदिन भोर भरि संभावित बाढ़ि के चेतावनी देलक अछि, किया कि नेपाल पर्यटन विभाग 64 अमेरिकी के सूची देखा रहल अछि जे एखन संपर्क सं बाहर अछि.

बाढ़ प्रभावित जिला के निवासी सब स हाई अलर्ट पर रहय के आग्रह कायल गेल अछि, भोटेकोशी नदी के जलस्तर बढ़ला के बाद।

रविदिन भोर भरि लोक के फोन पर बाढ़ि के चेतावनी मिलल. बुधदिन प्रलयकारी बाढ़ि सँ सबसँ बेसी प्रभावित क्षेत्र मे सँ एक क्षेत्र सँ काठमांडू केँ जोड़य बला एकटा पैघ राजमार्ग केँ बचाव दल साफ करबाक काज क’ रहल अछि।

समाचार पर और पढ़ें

नेपाली अधिकारीसबके ताजा जानकारीके अनुसार नेपाल आ तिब्बतमे मृत्युके संख्या ७५० स बेसी भऽ गेल अछि, आ ३ हजारसँ बेसी लोक लापता अछि ।

अमेरिकी अधिकारी गुरुवार क॑ कहलकै कि गुरुवार क॑ दुपहर तलक लगभग ९० अमेरिकी नागरिकऽ के हिसाब नै छै ।

नेपाल के पर्यटन विभाग द्वारा प्रकाशित सूची मे एखन 64 अमेरिकी संपर्क सं बाहर देखल गेल अछि.

लापता लोकनिक सूची मे सैकड़ों एहन लोक शामिल छथि जे एहि क्षेत्र मे काज करय लेल, कोनो पवित्र चोटी पर यात्रा करय लेल या नेपाल के पहाड़ देखय लेल आयल छलाह.

चीनी सरकारी मीडिया रविदिन कहलक जे तिब्बत मे 261 विदेशी लापता अछि।

बाढ़ि कोना खुलल

बुधदिन हिमालयी क्षेत्रमे हिमनदी ध्वस्त भेलाक बाद झटका बाढ़ि शुरू भेल अछि ।

द एसोसिएटेड प्रेस के हवाला सं अधिकारी आ जलवायु विशेषज्ञ के अनुसार ई आपदा बर्फ आ चट्टान के हिमस्खलन के बाद एकटा नदी के रोकला के बाद भेल छल, फेर अचानक नीचा के लहर उठल छल.

...

एकर बाद बाढ़ि रसुवा जिला मे गाम, सड़क आ जलविद्युत परियोजना कए फाड़ि देलक। एकर बाद बाढ़ि सीमाक चीनी कात धरि पहुँचि गेल।

रसुवा जिला में अगस्त 2025 में सेहो एहने बाढ़ि आयल छल.तखन पड़ोसी इलाका तिब्बत में एकटा हिमनदी झील पहाड़ी क्षेत्र में बेसी तापमान के बीच उमड़ि गेल छल.

नौ गोटेक मृत्यु भेल अछि, आ नेपाल आ चीन केँ जोड़य बला पुल सहित महत्वपूर्ण बुनियादी ढांचा क्षतिग्रस्त भेल अछि ।

हिमालय क्षेत्र बाढ़, भारी वर्षा आरू भूस्खलन के खास तौर प॑ कमजोर छै, कैन्हेंकि मानव के कारण जलवायु परिवर्तन के परिणामस्वरूप ई क्षेत्र बाकी दुनिया के तुलना म॑ तेजी स॑ गरम होय रहलऽ छै ।

काठमांडू स्थित संस्था इंटरनेशनल सेंटर फॉर इंटीग्रेटेड माउंटेन डेवलपमेंट केरऽ शोध म॑ पता चललै कि पूरा विशाल पहाड़ी हिन्दू कुश हिमालय (एचकेएच) क्षेत्र म॑ ग्लेशियर केरऽ बर्फ के नुकसान २००० स॑ दुगुना होय गेलऽ छै, जेकरऽ मुख्य कारण छै कि बढ़तऽ वैश्विक तापमान ।

एचकेएच म॑ अफगानिस्तान केरऽ ५०० मील के हिन्दू कुश प्रणाली शामिल छै आरू एकरऽ श्रृंखला मध्य आरू दक्षिण एशिया केरऽ आठ देशऽ म॑ लगभग २,१७५ मील तक फैललऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ पाकिस्तान, भारत, नेपाल, भूटान, चीन, बांग्लादेश आरू म्यांमार शामिल छै, जेकरा स॑ ई दुनिया केरऽ सबसें व्यापक आरू महत्वपूर्ण पर्वत प्रणाली म॑ स॑ एक छै ।

...

अमेरिकी परिवार लापता प्रियजन के बारे में बात करैत अछि |

बाढ़िक बादक परिणाम विनाशकारी रहल अछि, आ अनिश्चितता परिवारक लेल तड़पैत रहल अछि।

लांग आइलैंड केरऽ निवासी जिगीशा मोटवानी, जेकरऽ परिवार दशकों स॑ लापता यात्री जितेंद्र पटेल आरू अमिता अमीन क॑ जानत॑ छै, न॑ पहल॑ न्यूजवीक क॑ बतैलकै कि जब॑ ओकरा पता चललै कि ई लोगऽ के हिसाब-किताब नै करलऽ गेलऽ लोगऽ म॑ शामिल छै त॑ ओकरा “आंत” होय गेलै ।

मोटवानी कहलनि जे, ओ सब विस्तारित परिवार जेकाँ छथि। ओ कहली जे हमरा उम्मीद अछि जे हम सब हुनका स संपर्क मे आबि कए वापस अनबाक तरीका ताकि सकब।

संपर्क स॑ बाहर के रूप म॑ सूचीबद्ध लेक्सिंगटन केरऽ निवासी जीवन ज्योति केरऽ करीबी दोस्त मनमीत सिंह मीट न॑ न्यूजवीक क॑ बतैलकै कि हुनी ओकरा १५ साल स॑ भी अधिक समय स॑ जान॑ छै आरू ओकरऽ परिवार केरऽ भरण-पोषण म॑ मदद करी रहलऽ छै, कैन्हेंकि प्रियजन जवाब खोजै म॑ मदद करी रहलऽ छै ।

ओ कहलनि जे, ई बहुत हृदयविदारक अछि। "हम सभ क्लोजर लेब' के कोशिश क' रहल छी, अहाँ सभक संग बहुत ईमानदारी सँ कहब."

अधिकारियऽ न॑ अभी तलक ई बात के पुष्टि नै करलकै कि संपर्क स॑ बाहर के रूप म॑ सूचीबद्ध लोगऽ के लापता, घायल, फंसलऽ या अन्यथा आपदा के वजह स॑ संवाद करै म॑ असमर्थ होय के पुष्टि होय गेलऽ छै कि नै ।

राष्ट्रपति डोनाल्ड ट्रम्प आ द स्टेट डिपार्टमेंट नेपाल बाढ़ि के संबोधन

विदेश विभाग बुधदिन प्रकाशित प्रेस विज्ञप्ति मे कहलनि जे, नेपालक रसुवा जिला मे भेल विनाशकारी आकस्मिक बाढ़ि मे अपन जान गंवा चुकल लोकक परिवार आ प्रियजन के प्रति अमेरिका गहींर संवेदना व्यक्त करैत अछि।

"हमरऽ विचार ई आपदा स॑ प्रभावित सब के साथ छै ।"

विभाग न॑ नोट करलकै कि हुनी स्थिति प॑ नजर रखी रहलऽ छै आरू क्षेत्र म॑ आपदा प्रतिक्रिया सलाहकार क॑ तैनात करी देल॑ छै ।

विदेश विभाग न॑ कैथोलिक राहत सेवा के माध्यम स॑ ५ लाख डॉलर के सहायता देल॑ छै ।

न्यूजवीक न॑ नियमित काम के समय स॑ बाहर आरू जानकारी लेली विदेश विभाग स॑ संपर्क करलकै ।

...

गुरुवार क॑ ओवल ऑफिस म॑ पत्रकारऽ स॑ बात करतें हुअ॑ राष्ट्रपति डोनाल्ड ट्रंप न॑ कहलकै कि हम्में कोनो भी मदद के पेशकश करल॑ छियै जेकरऽ ओकरा जरूरत छै ।

"से त' क्रूर छल. एकदम एहन किछु कियो नहि देखने छल. मजबूत, नीक जकाँ बनल भवन सभ केँ एना मेटा देल गेल जेना दाँत-चुनमुनी हो. ई त' भयानक बात छैक." हम सब सहायता पठा रहल छी, आ नेतृत्व स बात केलहुं अछि, आ हुनका सब के ई बता दैत छी जे ओ जे किछु चाहैत छथि से होयत."

राष्ट्रपति आगू कहलनि जे, हुनका लग ओहि समय नेपाल मे रहनिहार अमेरिकी लोकनिक “पूर्ण सूची” नहि अछि।

ओ कहलनि जे, उम्मीद अछि जे ओ सब ठीक छथि, मुदा से एहन लागल जेना कियो हेरा जायत, दुर्भाग्यवश।

full_article:
LONDON -- The death toll from last week's flash flooding disaster in the Nepal-Tibet border region rose to at least 750 people as of Sunday, according to the latest updates from Nepali and Chinese officials.

At least 734 bodies had been recovered in Nepal as of Sunday, the Nepal National Disaster Management Authority said in a post to X. At least 2,498 people are still missing, the authority said.

On the other side of the border, China's state-run Xinhua News Agency said that at least 16 people had been confirmed killed. Another 546 people were still missing, Xinhua reported.

At least 90 Americans were still among the missing as of Friday, according to a State Department spokesperson. The department confirmed Friday that five Americans had been evacuated, up from three on Thursday.

Rescue works continue at Trishuli Center in Nepal's Nuwakot district on Aug. 30, 2026. Arun Sankar/AFP via Getty Images

Related Hundreds dead as over 3,000 remain missing in massive Nepal-Tibet flood

"There is no higher priority for us than the safety of American citizens," the State Department said in a statement on Saturday, saying U.S. embassies in Nepal and China were working to assist Americans and support disaster relief efforts.

In the statement, the State Department said it was "standing with the people of Nepal" and would provide "$3.6 million worth of life-saving humanitarian assistance, including up to three months of emergency food assistance to up to 10,000 flood-affected households."

The flooding, captured in dramatic video footage, occurred in the northern Rasuwa district along the border with Tibet at around 8:40 a.m. local time Wednesday, authorities said. The flooding inundated areas along the Trishuli River, burying some buildings and damaging bridges and roadways.

Popular Reads Dolly Parton’s sister reveals the singer’s touching final act of generosity Aug 27 'It stood like a serpent': American who survived deadly Nepal flood tells her story 1 day ago 'She was suffering': Hayden Panettiere's mom details relationship during final months Aug 24

The deadly wall of water that descended from the mountains on the border between Nepal and Tibet caused destruction at least 62 miles downriver from the border in Nepal, an ABC News analysis of verified video and satellite images shows.

This graphic shows destruction along the path of a landslide and subsequent flash flood along the Nepal-Tibet border. Felt Maps/ABC News

Related Nepal-Tibet flood deaths rise to 389 amid search for hundreds of missing tourists

The flood was reportedly triggered by a landslide about 12 miles northeast of the Rasuwagadhi border post along the Nepal-China frontier, according to Nepal Disaster Management.

A 5.2-magnitude landslide was registered in Nepal on Wednesday, according to the U.S. Geological Survey.

The initial location of the glacier was a cliff about 16,000 feet high. The debris avalanche, or landslide, slid down 6,000 feet on the slope, the USGS said.

title: Nepal warns of possible fresh flooding as communities grapple with devastation | World News | 2news.com - KTVN

full_article:
DHADING, Nepal (AP) — Authorities in Nepal warned of possible fresh flooding on Sunday and urged residents in flood-affected districts to remain on high alert after water levels rose in the Bhotekoshi River.

Flood warning notices were sent to people's phones early Sunday as rescue crews worked to clear a major highway connecting Kathmandu to one of the areas worst hit by Wednesday's catastrophic floods, which killed at least 800 people and left more than 3,000 missing in Nepal and Tibet.

In Dhading, one of the worst-hit regions in Nepal, some residents began returning to ruined homes to see what can be salvaged.

Residents sat in homes with walls washed away by the floods, shoveling sludge-like mud and rubble off balconies or window frames. Others scanned the ground for items they could pick out of the mud and rinse off. One man had returned for his chickens, which he found alive. He tied them up and put them in the cabin of his truck.

“Everything is finished. Nothing is left. Not even our home,” Sharmila Tamang, a Dhading resident who was trying to salvage items from her home, told The Associated Press.

At a key power plant that was severely damaged by the floods, workers started inspecting the facilities Sunday to survey the destruction. The plant serves over 20,000 people across four districts.

In the town of Galchhi, a group of residents sought higher ground on a nearby bridge and watched as the river roared by. Some pointed to enormous rocks washed downriver during the earlier floods, while others standing on a suspension bridge were warned off with whistles.

Along the river, homes, vehicles and farm tractors could be seen jutting from the thick gray-brown sediment that enveloped entire villages in some areas. Parts of rice terraces along the riverside had dropped into the river after landslides hit them.

Nepal’s disaster agency said Sunday the death toll had climbed to 788 with 2,502 missing, while Chinese authorities reported 16 deaths and 546 missing on the Chinese side of the border.

The missing include hundreds of people from over a dozen countries who were in the region to work, visit the mountains or make a pilgrimage to a sacred peak. On Sunday, Chinese state media said 261 foreigners were missing in Tibet, including over a hundred Nepalis and others from around the world.

Residents are receiving constant flood warnings

Homes and businesses left intact after the flooding were still without electricity on Sunday, as twisted power line poles and wires lay tangled in the mud.

Prithivi Highway is a crucial supply route for food, fuel and other goods entering Kathmandu from other parts of the country. While most of the highway is operational, other parts still face repair challenges.

The latest warnings came after Chinese authorities informed their Nepalese counterparts of increased water flow upstream, according to Dharam Raj Uprety, chief executive of Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority.

But residents of the flood-hit villages said they were struggling to make sense of near-constant alarms they've received since the initial floods.

“Sometimes they say a flood is coming, then we have to run again to higher ground, even at night. There is also rain,” said Govind Shreshta, a resident. “It’s really difficult for me. I have a 72-year-old father and 70-year-old mom. I must carry them and I am exhausted. It’s going on like this for those who are still alive.”

Large concrete and smaller suspension bridges were destroyed, leaving communities on the other side of the river with less easy access.

“Those who are there are now stuck there. Those who are here are stuck here. It’s going to be very difficult,” said Sattan Singh Tamang, 47, who was working near a bridge when Wednesday’s floods came.

Minister says Nepalis have become victims of climate change

Wednesday’s flash floods started after a glacial collapse high in the Himalayan region. Scientists who studied satellite images said bedrock underneath a glacier high in the Himalayan region had collapsed, taking part of the glacier with it. The rockfall was so extreme that it registered as magnitude 5.2.

The rocks and melted water then swelled the rivers in the valleys below, causing a torrent of water that swept buildings, bridges and earth downstream in Tibet and Nepal.

Nepal’s foreign minister called for a global response to climate change, saying Nepal was bearing a disproportionate share of its impact.

“Despite having only 0.1 percent contribution to the global emissions, people of Nepal have become major victims of climate change,” Shisir Khanal said Saturday.

Scientists have said it is too early to draw a direct connection between global warming and Wednesday’s catastrophe. However, they said that as Earth’s temperature rises because of human activities such as burning oil, gas and coal, the chances of such disasters increase, especially in the Himalayan mountains, which are warming considerably faster than many other parts of the world.

Meanwhile, Malaysia's Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said Sunday his country will send a search-and-rescue team to Nepal to assist with relief efforts and help evacuate Malaysians affected by the disaster.

Malaysia has also pledged $1 million in financial aid to Nepal, he said in a statement.

Associated Press writers Aijaz Hussain in New Delhi and Shristi Kafle in Kathmandu, Nepal, and video journalist Shonal Ganguly in Dhading, Nepal, contributed to this report.

नदी के कात में घर, गाड़ी आ खेत के ट्रैक्टर के मोट धूसर-भूरा रंग के तलछट सं निकलल देखल जा सकैत छल जे किछु इलाका में पूरा गाम के घेरने छल. नदी क कात मे चाउर क छत क किछु हिस्सा भूस्खलन क बाद नदी मे खसि गेल छल।

नेपाल केरऽ आपदा एजेंसी न॑ रविवार क॑ कहलकै कि मरै वाला के संख्या ७८८ होय गेलऽ छै आरू २,५०२ लोग लापता छै, जबकि चीनी अधिकारियऽ न॑ सीमा के चीनी तरफ स॑ १६ लोगऽ के मौत आरू ५४६ लोगऽ के लापता होय के खबर देल॑ छै ।

लापता लोगऽ म॑ दर्जन भर स॑ भी अधिक देशऽ के सैकड़ों लोग शामिल छै जे ई क्षेत्र म॑ काम करै, पहाड़ऽ के दौरा करै या कोनो पवित्र चोटी के तीर्थयात्रा करै लेली गेलऽ छेलै । रविदिन चीनी सरकारी मीडिया तिब्बत मे 261 विदेशी लापता अछि जाहि मे दुनिया भरिक सौ सं बेसी नेपाली आ अन्य लोक लापता अछि।

निवासी सब के लगातार बाढ़ के चेतावनी भेट रहल अछि

रविदिन बाढ़ि के बाद बरकरार छोड़ल गेल घर आ व्यवसाय एखनो बिजली के बिना छल, कियाकि बिजली लाइन के मुड़ल खंभा आ तार थाल मे उलझल पड़ल छल।

पृथ्वी राजमार्ग देशक अन्य भागसँ काठमाण्डौमे प्रवेश करयवला खाद्य, ईंधन आ अन्य सामानक लेल एकटा महत्वपूर्ण आपूर्ति मार्ग अछि । जखन कि अधिकांश राजमार्ग परिचालन मे अछि, मुदा अन्य हिस्सा कए एखनो मरम्मत क चुनौती क सामना करय पड़ैत अछि।

नेपाल केरऽ राष्ट्रीय आपदा जोखिम कम करै आरू प्रबंधन प्राधिकरण केरऽ मुख्य कार्यकारी धर्मराज उप्रेटी के अनुसार चीनी अधिकारियऽ न॑ अपनऽ नेपाली समकक्ष क॑ अपस्ट्रीम म॑ पानी केरऽ बहाव बढ़ला के जानकारी देला के बाद ताजा चेतावनी देलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

लेकिन बाढ़ स॑ प्रभावित गाँवऽ के निवासी न॑ कहलकै कि शुरुआती बाढ़ के बाद स॑ लगभग लगातार अलार्म मिलै वाला अलार्म के मतलब समझै लेली संघर्ष करी रहलऽ छै ।

निवासी गोविन्द श्रेष्ठ कहलनि जे, कखनो काल कहैत छथि जे बाढ़ि आबि रहल अछि, तखन फेर सँ ऊँच जमीन पर दौड़य पड़ैत अछि, ओहो राति मे, बरखा सेहो होइत अछि। "हमरा लेल ई सचमुच कठिन अछि. हमर एकटा 72 सालक पिता आ 70 सालक मम्मी छथि. हम हुनका सभ केँ जरूर ढोब' पड़त आ हम थक गेल छी. जे एखनो जीवित छथि हुनका लेल ई एना चलि रहल अछि."

पैघ कंक्रीट आ छोट झूला पुल नष्ट भ गेल, जाहि स नदी क दोसर कात क समुदाय कए कम आसानी स पहुंचल जा सकैत छल।

बुधदिन बाढ़ि अयला पर एकटा पुल के पास काज करय वाला 47 वर्षीय सत्तन सिंह तामांग कहलनि जे, जे ओतय छथि ओ आब ओतहि फंसल छथि, जे एतय छथि ओ एतय फंसल छथि, ई बहुत कठिन होयत।

मन्त्री कहलनि जे नेपाली जलवायु परिवर्तनक शिकार भेल अछि

बुधदिन के झटका बाढ़ि हिमालयी क्षेत्र मे उच्च हिमनदी गिरला के बाद शुरू भेल अछि. उपग्रह केरऽ तस्वीर के अध्ययन करै वाला वैज्ञानिक न॑ कहलकै कि हिमालय क्षेत्र केरऽ ऊँचऽ ग्लेशियर के नीचें के बेडरोक गिरी गेलऽ छै, जेकरा स॑ ग्लेशियर केरऽ कुछ हिस्सा भी अपनऽ साथ ल॑ गेलऽ छै । चट्टान केरऽ खसना एतना चरम पर छेलै कि एकरऽ परिमाण ५.२ के रूप में पंजीकृत होय गेलै ।

तखन चट्टान आ पिघलल पानि नीचा घाटी मे नदी कए फुला देलक, जाहि स पानिक धार बनल जे तिब्बत आ नेपाल मे भवन, पुल आ धरती कए नीचा बहरा गेल ।

नेपाल केरऽ विदेश मंत्री जलवायु परिवर्तन के प्रति वैश्विक प्रतिक्रिया के आह्वान करतें हुअ॑ कहलकै कि एकरऽ प्रभाव म॑ नेपाल केरऽ असमान हिस्सा छै ।

शिसिर खनाल शनिदिन कहलनि जे, वैश्विक उत्सर्जन मे मात्र 0.1 प्रतिशत योगदान रहला के बादो नेपाल के लोक जलवायु परिवर्तन के प्रमुख शिकार भ गेल अछि।

वैज्ञानिक सब के कहनाय छनि जे ग्लोबल वार्मिंग आओर बुधदिन के प्रलय के बीच सीधा संबंध बनाबय मे एखन जल्दबाजी अछि. लेकिन हुनकऽ कहना छै कि जेना-जेना मानवीय गतिविधि जैना कि तेल, गैस आरू कोयला जलाबै के वजह स॑ पृथ्वी केरऽ तापमान बढ़ी जाय छै, खास करी क॑ हिमालय केरऽ पहाड़ऽ म॑ ई तरह के आपदा के संभावना बढ़ी जाय छै, जे दुनिया केरऽ बहुत सारा अन्य भागऽ स॑ काफी तेजी स॑ गरम होय रहलऽ छै ।

एम्हर मलेशिया के प्रधानमंत्री अनवर इब्राहिम रविदिन कहलनि जे हुनकर देश राहत कार्य मे सहायता आ आपदा सं प्रभावित मलेशिया के लोक के बाहर निकालय मे मदद करय लेल खोज-बचाव टीम नेपाल भेजत.

मलेशिया नेपालके १० लाख डॉलरके आर्थिक सहयोगके प्रतिज्ञा सेहो कएलगेल ओ विज्ञप्तिमे बतौलनि अछि ।

एसोसिएटेड प्रेस के साहित्यकार नई दिल्ली में आइजाज हुसैन आ नेपाल के काठमांडू में श्रीस्टी काफ्ले, आ नेपाल के धडिंग में वीडियो पत्रकार शोनाल गांगुली के एहि रिपोर्ट में योगदान छलनि।

एसोसिएटेड प्रेस कें जलवायु आ पर्यावरण कवरेज कें कईटा निजी फाउंडेशनक सं आर्थिक सहायता भेटैत छै. सब सामग्री के लेल एपी के जिम्मेदारी मात्र अछि। परोपकार कें साथ काम करय कें लेल एपी कें मानक, समर्थक कें सूची आ वित्त पोषित कवरेज क्षेत्रक कें एपी.ओआरजी पर खोजूं.

title: Photos: Nepal issues alerts as region’s flash flood death toll reaches 750 - Al Jazeera
description: Photos: Nepal issues alerts as region’s flash flood death toll reaches 750  Al Jazeera
publisher.title: Al Jazeera
full_article:
Authorities in Nepal have warned of further flooding, urging residents in inundated districts to remain on high alert after water levels rose in the Bhotekoshi River.

Flood alerts were sent to mobile phones on Sunday morning as rescue teams worked to clear a main highway linking Kathmandu with one of the areas worst hit by Wednesday’s catastrophic flash flood.

The combined death toll in Nepal and China’s Tibet region has risen to 750, with more than 3,000 people still missing. Nepal’s disaster agency said the death toll there had climbed to 734, with 2,498 people missing, while Chinese authorities reported 16 deaths and 546 people unaccounted for, including more than 100 Nepalis and others from over a dozen countries.

The latest warnings followed a notice from Chinese authorities to their Nepali counterparts of increased water flow upstream, Dharam Raj Uprety, chief executive of Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, told The Associated Press news agency.

As many as 93,000 people in Nepal have been affected by the disaster, according to the Red Cross.

Nepal appealed on Saturday for international financial assistance, as well as specialised rescue support, including heavy-lift drones, DNA testing kits and body freezer units.

The United States and Canada said they would provide about $3.6m each in humanitarian assistance.

The United Kingdom has pledged $6.8m in aid, while the United Nations has released $2.5m in emergency funding.

The European Union on Friday promised $2.3m, and the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies allocated more than $1m and launched an emergency appeal for $31m.

Chinese President Xi Jinping on Friday offered Beijing’s assistance.

नेपालके अधिकारीसब भोटेकोशी नदीमे जलस्तर बढलाके बाद जलप्रलय जिल्लाके निवासीसभके उच्च सतर्क रहैके आग्रह करैत आरो बाढिक चेतावनी देने छै ।

बुधवार के भोर में बाढ़ के अलर्ट मोबाइल फोन पर भेजल गेल, कियाकि बचाव टीम बुधदिन के भयावह आकस्मिक बाढ़ि सं सब सं बेसी प्रभावित इलाका सं काठमांडू के जोड़य वाला मुख्य राजमार्ग के खाली करय के काज केलक.

नेपाल आरू चीन केरऽ तिब्बत क्षेत्र म॑ कुल मिला क॑ मरे वाला के संख्या ७५० होय गेलऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ अखनी तलक ३,००० स॑ भी अधिक लोग लापता छै । नेपाल केरऽ आपदा एजेंसी न॑ कहलकै कि वहाँ मरे वाला के संख्या ७३४ होय गेलऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ २,४९८ लोग लापता छै, जबकि चीनी अधिकारियऽ न॑ १६ लोगऽ के मौत आरू ५४६ लोगऽ के बेहिसाब होय के खबर देल॑ छै, जेकरा म॑ १०० स॑ भी अधिक नेपाली आरू एक दर्जन स॑ भी अधिक देशऽ के अन्य लोग भी शामिल छै ।

नेपाल केरऽ राष्ट्रीय आपदा जोखिम कम करै आरू प्रबंधन प्राधिकरण केरऽ मुख्य कार्यकारी धर्मराज उप्रेती न॑ द एसोसिएटेड प्रेस समाचार एजेंसी क॑ बतैलकै कि चीनी अधिकारियऽ न॑ अपनऽ नेपाली समकक्ष क॑ अपस्ट्रीम म॑ पानी के प्रवाह बढ़ै के नोटिस के बाद ताजा चेतावनी देलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

रेडक्रसके अनुसार नेपालमे ९३ हजार जनता एहि आपदासँ प्रभावित भेल अछि ।

नेपाल शनिदिन अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय आर्थिक सहायताक अपील केलक अछि, संगहि विशेष बचाव सहयोगक अपील केलक अछि, जाहि मे भारी लिफ्ट ड्रोन, डीएनए परीक्षण किट आ बॉडी फ्रीजर यूनिट शामिल अछि ।

अमेरिका आरू कनाडा न॑ कहलकै कि हुनी लगभग ३.६ मिलियन डॉलर के मानवीय सहायता देतै ।

यूनाइटेड किंगडम न॑ ६.८ मिलियन डॉलर के सहायता के वादा करल॑ छै, जबकि संयुक्त राष्ट्र न॑ आपातकालीन फंडिंग के रूप म॑ २.५ मिलियन डॉलर जारी करलकै ।

यूरोपीय संघ न॑ शुक्रवार क॑ २.३ मिलियन डॉलर के वादा करलकै, आरू इंटरनेशनल फेडरेशन आफ रेड क्रॉस आरू रेड क्रिसेंट सोसाइटी न॑ १ मिलियन डॉलर स॑ भी अधिक के आवंटन करी क॑ ३१ मिलियन डॉलर के आपातकालीन अपील शुरू करलकै ।

विज्ञापन

चीन के राष्ट्रपति शी जिनपिंग शुक्रदिन बीजिंग के मदद के पेशकश केलनि.

Helicopters airlift heavy machinery to assist in tunnel rescue published at 12:15 BST 12:15 BST The Nepali Army has just shared footage on X of helicopters airlifting heavy equipment to the flood-affected hydropower tunnel area. The machinery can be seen dangling from the end of a long rope. A separate video - also shared by the army - shows workers clearing debris near the Trishuli-3A tunnel. Image source, Nepali Army / X Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing Crews pump air into blocked tunnel where workers believed trapped published at 11:36 BST 11:36 BST Part of the rescue effort is focused on reaching workers believed to be trapped in hydropower tunnels, with efforts currently under way at the Trishuli-3A site. Home Minister Sudan Gurung shared an update on Facebook yesterday saying rescuers had managed to reach the "crown" of the tunnel and had started pumping air through a small hole. He said they would "now start digging and send a rescue team inside". In a separate update also issued yesterday, Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha said communication had so far not been established. Rain has complicated efforts, with Shrestha saying there was a risk the operation would need to be temporarily suspended due to "increasing water flow". India and China have both sent experts to help in tunnel operations. Of the 2,502 people reported missing overall, hundreds are workers at the country's hydropower projects, according to Nepal's disaster agency. The younger brother of one hydropower worker tells Reuters he has been searching for him for days "without getting any sleep". He adds: "I believe there are many other families like mine who are suffering." Reporting from Kathmandu A young girl who was rescued on Friday, two days after devastating flash floods in Nepal, has been reunited with her parents in hospital. Manisha, 5, is in a stable condition, an official at the Teaching Hospital in Kathmandu tells us. Rescue workers were near Syabrubesi in Ruswa district looking for survivors when they thought they could hear a cat stuck under the rubble. Sanju Khatri, a police officer with Nepal's Armed Police Force says teams searched the area and started removing debris. That's when they found Manisha, who was trapped under the rubble. It took about two hours to rescue her - the video below shows the moment she was pulled alive from the rubble. She was alive but barely responsive, the official explains. The rescue team called for a chopper but due to bad weather conditions they were not able to evacuate her. Teams then took her to the force's rescue camp and gave her water. Manisha regained consciousness after a while and they started feeding her boiled rice water to revive her. She was traumatised, but on Saturday afternoon she was flown to the Teaching Hospital's paediatric emergency department in Kathmandu. Live reporter Image source, Reuters A flooding expert warns that the immediate concern in Nepal and Tibet is that the flash floods have created new risks. Jeff Da Costa, researcher in flood early warning and disaster risk at the University of Reading, tells me that debris from the disaster has blocked rivers and formed new lakes upstream. Similarly, infrastructure in the area is seriously damaged, meaning that "a second flood does not have to be as large as the first to cause serious impacts," he says. Da Costa says monitoring how lakes and barriers in the area are changing and tracking where they may burst "now matters enormously". The researcher adds it is important for China and Nepal to share monitoring information as "what happens upstream can affect people across the border very quickly". "Information has to move just as quickly and lead to practical decisions on the ground," he adds. Da Costa also describes how climate change is important background context for the disaster because warming is changing glaciers, permafrost and slope stability across the Himalayas. But he says the disaster can not be attributed to climate change without further analysis. Australia reporter The sister of an Australian man missing in Nepal say they are "holding onto hope while also trying to prepare our hearts for whatever comes". Michael Keats, an outdoor educator from New South Wales, was initially thought to be away from the disaster zone, but relatives later learned he was at the immigration centre at the Nepal-Tibet border when the tragedy hit. His sister, Karen Hayley, describes him as "the absolute light of our lives" and says he was travelling through Nepal "as part of a deeply significant spiritual pilgrimage to Mount Kailash". "This was a journey Michael had planned, dreamed of and longed to experience for a long time," she wrote on Instagram. "Although we are painfully aware that Michael’s chances of survival may be slim our family is still desperately waiting for answers." She adds the family are "holding onto hope while also trying to prepare our hearts for whatever comes". China correspondent Image source, VCG via Getty Images Tibet, which China annexed in the 1950s, is one of the most strictly controlled regions in the country. It has long demanded greater autonomy and is heavily monitored because Beijing fears any signs of instability such as protests. That is why orders have come personally from the top leader Xi Jinping and why Premier Li Qiang visited the site on Thursday. It is rare for him to make a visit so soon after a major disaster. To get into Tibet requires a special visa and it is difficult, if not impossible, for foreign media to gain entry. Trying to contact people there is just as hard. This makes it very difficult for us to know what is happening and we are relying heavily on reports from Chinese state media. Pilgrims making their way from Nepal through Tibet to the sacred mountain of Mount Kailash need four separate permits, which includes special permission from the Chinese military. title: Fears of more flooding in Nepal, 100 Americans among the missing as rescue efforts step up - NBC News
description: Fears of more flooding in Nepal, 100 Americans among the missing as rescue efforts step up  NBC News
publisher.title: NBC News
full_article:
KATHMANDU — Authorities in Nepal have warned of the risk of further flooding after heavy rainfall, as China sheds light on the scale of the disaster in its Tibet region.

Five days after surging floodwaters from a glacier collapse buried communities across the region in thick mud, rescuers in Nepal were still struggling to reach devastated communities as the full scale of the destruction emerged.

“The disaster here is overwhelming,” Ferrin Cole, an operations director at the U.S.-based Crisis Response International, told NBC News on Sunday. “The flood that came down that mountain just wiped out cities. We’re going in as fast as we can to get people the help that they need.”

Cole said his team would be working to provide help to those in need a locate missing persons, but that working in mud “is actually pretty dangerous.”

“The longer that death and mud are together, diseases breed, and so we’re always just aware of that,” he added.

Approximately 100 Americans are among the missing across Nepal and China’s Tibet region, the State Department said Saturday.

01:11 How did the catastrophic Nepal-Tibet flood happen? 00:00 00:00

In Nepal, the death toll has risen to 752, with over 2,500 people still missing, including 592 foreign nationals, according to the country’s disaster agency. The Nepal Tourism Board said 261 foreign nationals have been rescued.

China has separately reported 16 deaths and 546 people missing in its Tibet region, including 261 foreign nationals. It is unclear how much overlap there is between the Chinese and Nepali missing-person counts.

Those missing loved ones may face a long wait for answers, with many bodies washed far downstream and recovered in poor condition. Morgues in Nepal have been overwhelmed, though authorities are collecting DNA samples in the hopes of notifying relatives.

In Nepal’s Chitwan district, where a number of bodies have washed up, police officer Anil Thapa told Reuters that “more than half” of recovered bodies were “beyond recognition.”

“Many have no visible faces. In some cases, only hands or legs remain,” the officer added.

Relatives of people missing after flash floods in Rasuwa and Nuwakot search for information at Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital on Aug. 30. Sanjit Pariyar / NurPhoto via Getty Images

The response is also being complicated by a landslide-dammed lake above the border checkpoint that is overflowing, while heavy rain in Nepal has pushed up river levels and prompted fresh warnings for people living along waterways.

Nepal’s Flood Alert system said Sunday that heavy rainfall had been measured in various watershed areas of Gandaki Province, and that the water levels were “expected to rise.”

“Therefore, people living in riverside areas are requested to adopt caution,” it said on X.

But in flood-hit areas, residents were struggling to make sense of repeated warnings since the initial floods.

“Sometimes they say a flood is coming, then we have to run again to higher ground, even at night. There is also rain,” Govind Shreshta, a resident of the town of Galchhi, told Associated Press. “It’s really difficult for me. I have a 72-year-old father and 70-year-old mom. I must carry them and I am exhausted. It’s going on like this for those who are still alive.”

Residents living along Trishuli River take shelter at higher ground after fleeing homes early in the morning, as authorities issue new flash flood warning, in Bidir, Nuwakot, Nepal, on Aug. 30. Daniel Ceng / Anadolu via Getty Images

China’s state-run media, CCTV, said Sunday that the event was part of a growing pattern of glacier-related disasters in the region, with the avalanche reaching China’s Gyirong Port within minutes of occurring.

“The disaster was caused by glacier instability resulting from the long-term effects of climate warming,” said Chinese state media.

“It struck suddenly, with a large peak flow, high speed, severe destructive force and a wide impact area,” the report added. “These are also new and significant characteristics of cryosphere-related disasters emerging across the Tibetan Plateau and surrounding regions.”

While it will take time to determine the exact cause of the mudslide and flood disaster, analysts say climate change is likely to have played a role.

The Himalayan region, which includes Nepal, India, Pakistan, Bhutan, China and Afghanistan, is among the places most vulnerable to climate change in the world, with temperatures rising faster than the global average. The warmer conditions are accelerating glacial melt, further destabilizing a region that is already prone to floods, landslides and earthquakes.

The suspected collapse of a melting glacier shook the ground so violently that seismic monitors initially registered it as a magnitude-4.4 earthquake.

The U.S. Geological Survey later revised that number to the equivalent of a magnitude-5.2 earthquake and said a second seismic event three hours after the first registered as the equivalent of a 4.2 temblor. Debris flow and flooding from what it called a “slope failure” travelled 62 miles, the USGS said.

“We will not be able to attribute 100% that this is because of climate change, because these changes have been happening” over a long period of time, Neera Shrestha Pradhan, an expert at Nepal’s International Center for Integrated Mountain Development, said on Friday. But climate change might be breaking a threshold, she said, and “maybe that might be one of the causes of this happening.”

full_article:
By Deborah Castellano Lubov

“From Haiti come terrible reports of the grave massacre perpetrated in Kenscoff, in which numerous people have lost their lives while others have been kidnapped. I express my prayerful closeness to the victims and their families and ask that all the hostages be released without delay. I make a heartfelt appeal to all those responsible to make a concrete commitment to ensuring the safety of the population and putting an end to every form of violence.”

Pope Leo XIV made the appeal following the recitation of the Angelus prayer on Sunday at noon in Castel Gandolfo, where he stayed overnight after taking part Saturday evening in the Marian procession of Our Lady of the Lake on Lake Albano.

Massacre and desperation in Kenscoff {"@context": "http://schema.org","@type": "ImageObject","contentUrl": "https://www.vaticannews.va/content/dam/vaticannews/agenzie/images/reuters/2026/08/24/23/1787605203307.JPG/_jcr_content/renditions/cq5dam.thumbnail.cropped.750.422.jpeg","creditText": "Vatican News","height": "750","width": "422"}

Alleviate the suffering of Nepal and Tibet

Following the appeal for Haiti, Pope Leo assured those affected by the devastating flooding in Nepal and Tibet of his prayers. He invited the faithful to pray for those who have died, the injured and missing, their families, and the rescuers involved in the ongoing emergency response.

“May everyone’s concern and commitment," he prayed, "help to alleviate suffering and bring the necessary assistance to the affected populations.”

The Vatican announced Saturday that Pope Leo, through the Dicastery for the Service of Charity, had sent financial assistance to Caritas Nepal to help meet the most urgent needs of people affected by the disaster.

Death toll exceeds 700 and thousands displaced

In coordination with the Apostolic Nunciature of Nepal, the Pope’s contribution will support Caritas Nepal, which operates under the direction of the Apostolic Vicariate, in its relief efforts. These began in the first hours following the disaster and include providing food, basic necessities, and shelter to people who have lost everything.

Relief operations are continuing as the death toll in the affected regions rises, with more than 700 people reported dead between Nepal and Tibet and at least 3,000 still missing.

In a telegram sent Thursday and signed by Cardinal Secretary of State Pietro Parolin, Pope Leo expressed his sorrow over the loss of life and widespread destruction. He commended the souls of those who died “to the clemency of the Almighty” and offered his heartfelt condolences to the bereaved.

He also assured those affected by the disaster of his spiritual closeness and prayed for the emergency personnel engaged in ongoing search-and-rescue operations.

A renewed appeal for peace

Pope Leo then urged the faithful to continue praying for peace, recalling the words of Saint Augustine, whose liturgical memorial was celebrated on August 28.

The Pope recalled Augustine’s image of peace as being like “the bread of the miracle that grew in the hands of the disciples as they broke it and distributed it.”

“May the number increase throughout the world,” he prayed, “of those who courageously break and distribute the bread of peace, overcoming divisions, promoting justice, and practicing forgiveness, for the good of all.”

Prayer for Creation

Finally, the Holy Father recalled in English that on Tuesday, September 1, the Church will celebrate the World Day of Prayer for the Care of Creation.

“This marks the beginning of the Season of Creation – observed by Christians of various denominations – whose theme this year is ‘Living Water.’”

“As I recalled in the Message for this Day,” Pope Leo reiterated, “caring for our common home calls for a conversion of heart, so that what has been used to bring about destruction may instead be directed toward life.”

“I invite everyone to join in prayer and action, that we may become channels of the living water of God’s peace, refreshing our wounded world.”

DHADING, Nepal (AP) — Authorities in Nepal warned of possible fresh flooding on Sunday and urged residents in flood-affected districts to remain on high alert after water levels rose in the Bhotekoshi River.

Flood warning notices were sent to people’s phones early Sunday as rescue crews worked to clear a major highway connecting Kathmandu to one of the areas worst hit by Wednesday’s catastrophic floods , which killed at least 800 people and left more than 3,000 missing in Nepal and Tibet.

In Dhading, one of the worst-hit regions in Nepal, some residents began returning to ruined homes to see what can be salvaged.

Residents sat in homes with walls washed away by the floods, shoveling sludge-like mud and rubble off balconies or window frames. Others scanned the ground for items they could pick out of the mud and rinse off. One man had returned for his chickens, which he found alive. He tied them up and put them in the cabin of his truck.

Wednesday’s flash floods started after a glacial collapse high in the Himalayan region. Scientists who studied satellite images said bedrock underneath a glacier high in the Himalayan region had collapsed, taking part of the glacier with it. The rockfall was so extreme that it registered as magnitude 5.2 .

The rocks and melted water then swelled the rivers in the valleys below, causing a torrent of water that swept buildings, bridges and earth downstream in Tibet and Nepal.

Nepal’s foreign minister called for a global response to climate change, saying Nepal was bearing a disproportionate share of its impact.

“Despite having only 0.1 percent contribution to the global emissions, people of Nepal have become major victims of climate change,” Shisir Khanal said Saturday.

Scientists have said it is too early to draw a direct connection between global warming and Wednesday’s catastrophe. However, they said that as Earth’s temperature rises because of human activities such as burning oil, gas and coal, the chances of such disasters increase, especially in the Himalayan mountains, which are warming considerably faster than many other parts of the world.
